title: This Week in Finance & Tech
body:
The tech world has been busy this week, particularly with OpenAI. The company is removing rate limits for free ChatGPT users, meaning you will soon have unlimited access to text chats. On the hardware front, reports suggest their upcoming AI device will be a smart speaker priced between $300 and $400. Meanwhile, OpenAI is pushing back in its trade secrets case against Apple, arguing that Apple's own security practices weaken their claims.

In financial news, President Donald Trump is renewing his attempt to remove Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook. This move is part of a broader strategy to reshape the central bank's board.

Elsewhere, Google Wallet is rolling out a feature that lets parents set up secure balances for their children, aimed at helping kids learn financial management with built-in safeguards. In the UK, Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced new powers for councils to restrict the number of vape and betting shops in town centres, citing concerns over the decline of local high streets.

Looking at the broader markets, U.S. stock futures are holding steady as investors wait for upcoming inflation data. There is also ongoing caution regarding the Middle East, as Prime Minister Burnham warned that the conflict could impact UK economic growth due to rising energy costs and supply chain disruptions.
